component.name: Cursor Speak
component.summary: Reads new Cursor CLI replies out loud

description.p: Cursor Speak sits in the system tray, watches your Cursor CLI (cursor-agent) chats, and reads each finished reply out loud. Code blocks, commands, file paths and tool output are left out, and headings and bullets are read as plain sentences.

ul.li: Reads only the final reply of each turn, never in-progress text
Watches every chat, so a new session works without any setup
Never speaks old replies when it starts
Opens chat files read-only and never touches the Cursor process
Local neural voice (piper), downloaded on first run, with espeak-ng as a fallback
Push-to-talk voice input: speak to start a new cursor-agent session or type into a running one, recognised locally with faster-whisper

description.p: Adds push-to-talk voice input. A keyboard shortcut (or the Talk button) records your voice, faster-whisper turns it into text on your computer, and the text opens a new cursor-agent session or is typed into the focused window with ydotool. Speech is paused while you talk.

Shows a main window on launch, starts hidden only at login, and ships a self-contained AppImage with Python and GTK 3 so it runs on Ubuntu 22.04 and newer without host PyGObject. First-run piper setup no longer blocks the window; espeak-ng or spd-say is used when piper cannot be installed.
Adds an AppImage build and an AppStream description.
